search.emptyText: Add NZBGeek, NZBFinder, DrunkenSlug, or another Newznab-compatible indexer with its API key.
search.hintAll: Searches run in parallel across all your indexers.
search.hintDedup: Releases repeated across indexers are shown only once.

search.saveNzbTitle: Save the .nzb file to your PC

subtitleDownload.other: Search your {n} indexers at once and download in one click.

server.connectionsHint: Check the maximum your plan allows. More connections isn't always faster.

servers.emptyText: Add your Usenet provider's NNTP credentials to start downloading.
servers.subtitle: Your Usenet providers. Backup servers are only used when the primary is missing an article.
servers.tip: Servers with the same priority share the work. If an article isn't on the primary, backup servers are checked in order.

settings.abortHopelessDesc: If more articles are missing than PAR2 can repair, the download stops so it doesn't waste data.
settings.addPausedDesc: New downloads don't start until you resume them.
settings.animationsDesc: Turn them off if you prefer a plainer interface or your computer is slow.
settings.askDestination: Ask where to save each NZB
settings.askDestinationDesc: Shows the destination window when adding files or links.
settings.associateDesc: Double-clicking a .nzb adds it to the queue.
settings.clipboardDesc: When you copy a link to a .nzb, you'll be asked whether to add it. Nothing is ever downloaded without confirmation.
settings.clipboardInspectDesc: Downloads the NZB to show its name and size before adding it. Some indexers count this as a grab (it isn't requested again when added).
settings.clipboardShow: Show the window when a link is detected
settings.clipboardShowDesc: If Nebula is in the tray, it opens automatically. Otherwise, a notification is shown.
settings.closeToTrayDesc: Closing the window doesn't stop downloads. To quit, use the tray icon menu.
settings.debridConnsDesc: Simultaneous HTTPS downloads, in 32 MB chunks. More connections usually mean more speed.
settings.debridDelete: Delete from the service when done
settings.debridDeleteDesc: Removes the download from your debrid account once it's on your PC (frees up space and download slots).
settings.debridNone: TorBox (Pro plan) or Premiumize, with its API key.
settings.dedupDesc: If the same release is on several indexers (even if it was reuploaded), it's shown only once and downloaded from the preferred one.
settings.deleteArchivesDesc: Deletes the .rar/.7z/.zip files once extraction succeeds.
settings.downloadWithDesc: NNTP uses your Usenet servers. Debrid sends the NZB to {name} and downloads the files from its servers, usually much faster. You can pick a different method when adding each NZB.
settings.downloadWithDescMany: NNTP uses your Usenet servers. Debrid sends the NZB to {name} (or the next one if it fails) and downloads the files from its servers, usually much faster. You can pick a different method when adding each NZB.
settings.downloadWithNone: Add a debrid service (TorBox Pro or Premiumize) to download through it.
settings.extractDesc: RAR, 7z, ZIP, and split volumes with the built-in 7-Zip.
settings.fallbackNntp: If the debrid service fails, download over NNTP
settings.fallbackNntpDesc: The other debrid services in the list are tried first (if the method was chosen automatically).
settings.featIndexersDesc: Search your Newznab indexers from Nebula.
settings.featNntpDesc: Download, repair, and extract with your Usenet provider or a debrid service (TorBox, Premiumize). If turned off, search can only save .nzb files to your PC.
settings.historyLimitDesc: The oldest ones are removed from the list automatically.
settings.indexersDesc: URL, API key, and priority for each indexer.
settings.jobFolder: Create a subfolder for each download
settings.jobFolderDesc: Uses the NZB name as a folder inside the destination.
settings.keepOneFeature: At least one feature must stay enabled.
settings.languageDesc: Uses the Windows language by default. Also changes the tray menu and notifications.
settings.legal: Includes 7-Zip © Igor Pavlov (GNU LGPL + unRAR restriction) and par2cmdline-turbo (GNU GPL v2), run as separate programs. Server passwords are encrypted with Windows Data Protection (DPAPI).
settings.minimizeToTrayDesc: The minimize button hides the window next to the clock.
settings.noNntpNote: You have no active NNTP servers: {name} will be used until you add one.
settings.nzbAsk: Ask for the folder every time
settings.nzbDirDesc: Where files are saved with the “.nzb” button (can be another program's watch folder).
settings.par2Desc: The original files and only the PAR2 index are downloaded first; recovery volumes are requested only if there's damage. Off: no PAR2 files are downloaded.
settings.patternsDesc: Besides links ending in .nzb, links containing any of these strings are detected (useful for indexers).
settings.quickAddDesc: The Download button adds the result to the queue with the default folder and options. Off: a window opens so you can choose the destination and options.
settings.retriesDesc: How many times an article is retried on the same server if the connection fails.
settings.searchLimitDesc: Per search; you can load more from the results list.
settings.tempDirDesc: Where in-progress downloads are stored. Empty = “_incomplete” subfolder in the destination (faster when finishing).
settings.timeoutDesc: Seconds without a response before the connection is considered dropped.
settings.hapticsDesc: A short vibration confirms what you tap and what you press and hold.

stats.articlesTip: Articles the server had: {ok} found, {missing} unavailable

ix.hint: Time of each request and results on the first page of each search.
ix.noData: No searches in this period. They're recorded starting with this version.

stats.noData: No finished downloads in this period.
stats.noServerDetail: Downloads from before this version didn't record which server was used, so they only count toward the overall rate.
stats.serversHint: NZBs each server took part in and how many finished successfully.
stats.subtitle: Success rate of your NZB downloads.

wizard.askDestination: Ask where to save each manually added NZB
wizard.closeToTray: Stay in the tray when the window is closed
wizard.debridHint: Using TorBox (Pro plan) or Premiumize? Click “Skip” if you don't have a Usenet provider, and add your API key later in the Debrid tab.
wizard.dedupDesc: The same release uploaded to several indexers appears only once.
wizard.doneNntp: Drag a .nzb onto the window, paste a link, or copy one to the clipboard to get started.
wizard.doneSearch: Go to Search to find whatever you want on {target}.

wizard.featuresTitle: What do you want to use?

wizard.indexersDesc: Search NZBGeek, NZBFinder, DrunkenSlug, and other Newznab indexers at once, without duplicates.

mode.indexers: You'll search your indexers and save .nzb files to your PC to use with another program.
mode.nntp: You'll add .nzb files from files, links, or the clipboard, and Nebula will download them from Usenet.
mode.none: Enable at least one feature to continue.

wizard.nntpDesc: Download, repair, and extract NZBs with your Usenet provider's credentials.
wizard.noApiKey: Without an API key, most indexers won't return any results.
wizard.noUsername: You haven't entered a username: most providers require one.
wizard.nzbDirHint: You can use another program's watch folder so it picks them up automatically.
wizard.prefsLead: You can change all of this anytime in Settings.
wizard.quickAddDesc: Adds the result straight to the queue, with no extra windows.
wizard.serverLead: Enter the NNTP details your provider gave you. You can add backup servers later.
wizard.serverRequired: Enter the NNTP server address (or click “Skip”).
wizard.welcomeText: Search your indexers and download from Usenet with automatic verification, repair, and extraction. We'll have you set up in a minute.

update.title: New version of Nebula
update.permission: To install it, allow Nebula to install apps on the screen that just opened, then come back.
update.androidHint: If you closed the Android installer, tap Install to open it again.
update.restarting: Installing… Nebula will close and reopen already updated.
update.activeDownloads: Active downloads will resume when Nebula reopens.
update.manualOnly: There's no automatic install for this system: the release page will open.
update.availableDesc: You can install it now or whenever you like from here.
update.upToDateDesc: You're on the latest version. Last checked: {time}.
update.neverChecked: Check GitHub for a new version.
update.autoDesc: When Nebula opens and every few hours. You'll get a window you can close.
update.skippedDesc: You won't be notified about this version; you can still install it from here.

api.title: Newznab and SABnzbd API
api.enableDesc: Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr and other programs can search all your indexers through Nebula (like NZBHydra2) and use Nebula as a SABnzbd download client.
api.addressDesc: As a Newznab indexer in Sonarr, Radarr or Prowlarr, together with the API key.
api.keyDesc: Apps send it with every request. If you change it, update it there too.
api.regenerated: New API key generated: update it in the apps that use the API.
api.portDesc: Port the API listens on (5077 by default).
api.lan: Allow connections from the local network
api.lanDesc: Other devices (a NAS, another PC…) can use it with the API key. When off, only this computer can.
api.noIndexers: With no active indexers the Newznab search returns nothing; the SABnzbd API works anyway.
api.docsDesc: How to connect it to Sonarr, Radarr or Prowlarr and what it supports.
api.androidNote: On Android the API only answers while Nebula is open or downloading.

sab.title: SABnzbd download client
sab.desc: Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Readarr and Prowlarr send NZBs to Nebula, follow the download and import it when it finishes.
sab.step1: In Sonarr or Radarr: Settings → Download Clients → + → SABnzbd.
sab.step2: Fill in these values (the category must exist in Nebula):
sab.step3: Press Test and save. What Sonarr sends shows up in Downloads with its category.
sab.noCategories: You don't have categories yet: create tv and movies so Sonarr and Radarr can use them.
sab.lanHint: If Sonarr or Radarr run on another computer or in Docker, turn on "Allow connections from the local network".
sab.docs: Supported modes and differences from SABnzbd

transfer.scanDesc: Scan the QR code Nebula shows on the other device to get its settings or send it yours.
transfer.sendDesc: Shows a QR code with your servers, indexers, debrid services and preferences to scan with the other device.
transfer.receiveDesc: Shows a QR code so your phone can send you its settings over Wi-Fi.
transfer.pasteDescShort: If you can't scan, paste the code copied on the other device.
transfer.pasteDesc: On the other device, open “Send my settings”, tap “Copy code” and get it over here (for example, in a message to yourself). Then paste it here.
transfer.sendTitle: Scan it with the other device
transfer.sendHint: In Nebula on the other device: Settings › Move to another device › Scan QR code.
transfer.secret: The QR code and the code include your passwords and API keys: don't share them with anyone.
transfer.tooBig: Your settings don't fit in a QR code. Copy the code and paste it on the other device.
transfer.receiveHint: In Nebula on your phone: Settings › Move to another device › Scan QR code. Both must be on the same Wi-Fi.
transfer.expired: The QR code has expired. Make a new one to continue.
transfer.firewall: If Windows asks about the firewall, allow access so your phone can connect.
transfer.importNote: This replaces the servers, indexers, debrid services and preferences on this device. Folders, history and system-specific options stay as they are.
transfer.pushText: They'll be sent encrypted over Wi-Fi to the device at {address}. You'll confirm the import there.
transfer.sent: Settings sent. Confirm them on the other device.
transfer.cameraDenied: Nebula needs permission to use the camera to scan the QR code.
transfer.scanHint: Point at the QR code Nebula shows on the other device
transfer.wizardLink: Already using Nebula on another device? Bring your settings over with a QR code

remote.enableDesc: Lets the Nebula Android app see and manage this PC's queue over the local network: add NZBs, pause, resume, move and delete downloads and change the speed limit. It can never touch the settings.
remote.addressDesc: On the same Wi-Fi the phone finds it by itself. Otherwise add it by hand with this address.
remote.portDesc: Remote control TCP port (5078 by default). Network search always uses UDP 5078.
remote.firewallNote: The first time, Windows asks whether Nebula may use the network: allow it on private networks.
remote.revokeText: That phone will no longer be able to control this PC. To use it again you'll have to pair it again.
remote.noPhones: No paired phones. On the phone, go to Settings → Control a PC.
remote.intro: While you control a PC, Downloads, History and Statistics show its own. First turn on “Remote control” in Nebula's settings on the PC.
remote.forgetText: This phone will stop controlling that PC. To do it again you'll have to pair it again.
remote.allPaired: The PCs found are already paired.
remote.noneFound: No PC found. Check that the PC has “Remote control” turned on and is on the same Wi-Fi, or add it by hand.
remote.manualDesc: The PC's IP and port, for example 192.168.1.20:5078. Away from home, with Tailscale, use its 100.x IP.
remote.pairingCheck: Check that {name} shows this same code and accept there:
remote.offline: No connection to {name}: it may be off, asleep or have Nebula closed.
remote.pairText: {name} ({from}) wants to control Nebula on this PC. Accept only if the phone shows the code {code}.

rss.subtitle: Automatically grab what your indexers and feeds publish, based on your rules.
rss.ruleSubtitle: What to grab, from which feeds and how to download it
rss.androidNote: On Android, RSS rules only work while Nebula is open. If you close the app or it stays in the background for a long time, nothing is checked until you come back.
rss.pausedNote: The queue is paused: no feed is checked until you resume it.
rss.noFeedsNote: Turn on indexer search or add an RSS URL to get feeds.
rss.noFeedLeft: None of its feeds exist anymore
rss.emptyText: Create a rule with the words you care about and Nebula will grab new releases as soon as they appear.
rss.feedsHint: Each indexer offers its feed of new releases. A feed is only checked if an active rule uses it, and every check counts in the indexer's stats.
rss.noFeeds: No feeds. Add an indexer or an RSS URL.
rss.logEmpty: Nothing has been grabbed automatically yet.
rss.nothingToCheck: No active feed is used by your rules
rss.badSize: The minimum size is larger than the maximum
rss.removeRuleMessage: "{name}" will stop grabbing releases. The log is kept.
rss.removeFeedMessage: {name} will no longer be checked and will be removed from the rules that use it.
rss.mustHelp: All of them must appear as whole words, ignoring case and dots. Use quotes for phrases: "web dl".
rss.mustRegexHelp: Matched against the full title, case-insensitive.
rss.destHelp: Empty = the category's folder. The folder isn't moved to other devices.
rss.onlyNewDesc: Only grab what's published after the rule was created ({date}).
rss.previewHint: See which items in the current feeds would match and why.

date.ok: Published after the rule was created
date.no: Published before the rule was created

why.duplicate: Already in the queue or history: will be skipped

finish.title: On finish
finish.desc: Actions that run when a download completes, when it fails or when the queue becomes empty. They never slow down downloads, and if something fails the reason goes to the Log.

kindDesc.discord: Message to a channel through a webhook
kindDesc.telegram: Message from your bot to a chat
kindDesc.ntfy: Push notification on your ntfy server
kindDesc.power: Shut down, sleep or hibernate when the queue is empty

finish.webhookHint: Receives a JSON POST: event, name, status, path, size, durationSecs, avgSpeed, via, error, stage and message.
finish.onceDesc: Turns itself off after it runs.
finish.powerNote: Only when the queue is empty (no paused or waiting jobs). There's a 60 s countdown first that you can cancel from the window, the notification or the tray.
finish.encrypted: Tokens and URLs are stored encrypted.
finish.testPower: Countdown test: nothing will shut down this time.

quick.title: When the queue is empty
quick.once: Just this once: turns itself off after it runs.
quick.armed: {action} when the queue is empty, just this once

countdown.shutdown: The PC is about to shut down
countdown.sleep: The PC is about to sleep
countdown.hibernate: The PC is about to hibernate
countdown.sub: The download queue is empty. Happening in {secs} s.
countdown.test: This is a test: nothing will happen at the end.

cats.defaultDesc: Fixed: uses the download folder and the global options
cats.desc: Every download goes into a category that sets its folder, how it's downloaded, its priority and its post-processing. Sonarr, Radarr and RSS rules can pick one, and indexer results go on their own to the one that matches their Newznab category.
cats.dirPlaceholder: Empty = download folder; relative = inside it
cats.newznabHelp: Newznab categories: numbers or ranges separated by commas (5000-5999 is TV, 2000-2999 movies). If several match, the narrowest range wins.
cats.presets: Create tv, movies, audio and books
cats.removeConfirm: Remove the "{name}" category? What's already in the queue or history keeps its name.
cats.ruleHelp: Sets the folder, priority and post-processing of what this rule grabs (the rule's own folder and method win if you set them).

web.setupDesc: This is the first time you open this Nebula. The username and password protect the web interface; the password must have at least {n} characters.
web.accountDesc: The session lasts 30 days in this browser. Changing the password signs out every session.
web.apiNote: Sonarr, Radarr and Prowlarr can use this same port: {url} (or /sabnzbd/api) with the key below.
web.toolFound: Using {path}. Leave it empty to find it automatically.
web.toolMissing: Not found ({path}). Install it or say where it is: without it downloads aren't repaired or extracted.
